newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica local govt debtors face legal action - paper.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica local govt debtors face legal action - paper.

text.p: South Africa's central government is refusing to bail out local authorities that have defaulted on their debts, leaving municipal debtors to face legal action, Business Day newspaper said on Wednesday.
The paper quoted major creditors as saying that final demands were being sent to defaulting muncipalities and they were studying which assets they would be allowed to attach once a judgment was made.
However, the amounts involved are small and the situation appears to have stabilised.

Nick Christodoulou, general manager of Sanlam which holds 2.7 billion rand of municipal debt, said his organisation was drafting final letters of demand. But he added only 20 million rand of debt had been affected and arrears amounted to two million rand.
The finance department reiterated that it would not bail out defaulting local government borrowers, adding it was illegal for them to finance operational deficits with bank overdrafts.
